mentions.story: P vs NP: The most important unsolved problem in computer science
mentions.text:
> - “p” - a category of problems which can be solved in O(n²)

> - “np” - a category of problems which can be checked, but not solved, in O(n²)

These definitions are incorrect. Certainly there are other polynomials than just n². P is the complexity class wherein the problem can be solved on a Turing machine in a number of steps equal to some polynomial of the size of the input. For NP, replace "Turing machine" with "nondeterministic Turing machine" and otherwise it's the same. The 'size of the input' is the count of symbols on the machine's tape, allowing for the input to be written in any finite alphabet, chosen by the designer of the Turing machine.

Nondeterministic can mean different…

mentions.story: Ask HN: How Sound Is the “Teach Yourself CS” Learning Resource?
mentions.text:
CS graduate here.

Can confirm this site is legit. These are all standard recommended texts in CS curriculum.

You could probably substitute SICP with other modern language text books on programming, but you're not really starting from square one so I'd skip to data structures and algorithms.

That being said, from my limited experience with SICP, it's very good. Even the old MIT lectures are good. And it gives you exposure to a functional language.

The only thing glaringly missing is computational theory which you can acquire this by going here:
